subject: Service degradation in APAC/US — temporary traffic shift and suggested steps
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@brightpay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: API errors from APAC region - urgent

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing 5xx errors and timeouts for token-based generation requests from our APAC region (Singapore) around 07:45 SGT. The errors are intermittent but persistent — our customers experience partial failures when running payroll jobs.

Can you confirm if this is on your side and whether there is a recommended quick fix? Our SREs are standing by.

- Emily
Engineering Manager, BrightPay

---
Attachment: screenshot-500s.png (image/png)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@brightpay.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: API errors from APAC region - urgent

Emily — thanks for flagging this. I'm opening an incident with the infra team now and looping in ops. Can you share:

- timestamps (UTC) when you saw failures
- a sample request id(s) if available

In the meantime, two immediate mitigation options we can offer:
1) Short-term: shift traffic from our APAC endpoint to US-west with Geo-failover (adds ~80–120ms RTT but should restore success rate).
2) Short-term alternate: call the regional fallback endpoint we can provision for your account (no code changes, just a DNS update we manage).

We will stay on this until your jobs are green. I will set a call with our SREs in ~20 minutes unless you prefer chat.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T08:35:00Z
Subject: [Incident] APAC service degradation — initial findings and recommended traffic shift

Team — initial probe: provider-side network egress from apac-1 (third-party cloud region) shows packet loss to several AZs. We are seeing increased tail latency and connection resets to our apac inference pool. Impact window starting ~2028-07-12T07:40Z.

Immediate recommendations for BrightPay (low-friction):
- Option A: Apply our managed DNS override to route BrightPay's APAC calls to us-west-2 pool. We can push this and monitor for 5–10 minutes; expected latency increase 80–130ms.
- Option B: Enable the per-account fallback we keep for enterprise customers (we already have it configured for BrightPay but disabled). Enabling is a config flip in the control plane — no DNS change required.

I will prepare a short step-by-step doc (rw-traffic-shift-quicksteps.pdf) and a condensed runbook. Karthik, you should propose Option B to the customer with Option A as fallback.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: incident-log-20280712.txt (text/plain)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@brightpay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T08:50:00Z
Subject: RE: Service degradation in APAC/US — temporary traffic shift and suggested steps

Emily — quick update and recommendation:

We've confirmed a transient networking degradation in the APAC provider region. To minimize customer impact, we recommend enabling your per-account fallback (Option B). This is a configuration flip on our side and does not require changes to your code or DNS. Expected outcome: complete recovery of successful calls within ~90–180s, with no client changes.

If you prefer DNS-based routing (Option A) we can do that too — expect slightly higher latency but also acceptable.

Please reply CONFIRM to proceed with Option B and we will enact immediately and monitor.

Thanks —
Karthik

Subject: Re: Service degradation in APAC/US — temporary traffic shift and suggested steps

CONFIRM. Please enable the fallback. We'll keep our SREs on standby and provide request ids if more errors occur. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, se an_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-15T16:42:00Z
Subject: Postmortem: Targeted APAC egress disruption — summary and customer follow-up

Team / BrightPay (cc'd in case we missed anyone),

Summary (condensed):
- Incident window: 2028-07-12T07:40Z -> 2028-07-12T09:10Z (primary impact to apac-1 egress).
- Root cause: transient packet loss due to a third-party network provider maintenance activity that did not follow announced routing policies; resulted in increased TCP resets to our apac inference fleet.
- Customer impact: BrightPay saw increased 5xx/timeout rates for ~90 minutes; business-critical payroll jobs were partially affected.

What we did:
- Enabled per-account fallback for BrightPay at 2028-07-12T08:59Z (Option B). This restored successful request rates within the 2–3 minute stabilization window.
- Provided a managed DNS workaround for customers requesting regional routing (Option A) as an alternative.
- Communicated with BrightPay during the incident and provided logs.

Action items (owners):
- (jonas_weber) Work with network provider to obtain detailed routing/maintenance timeline and request improved notification policies (ETA 2028-07-20).
- (monica_patel) Follow-up with BrightPay CS: share full logs (redacted), supply the postmortem doc, and offer a 10% service credit for the impacted day (discretionary approval obtained) (ETA 2028-07-16).
- (sean_gallagher) Validate that our fallback flip procedure has automated verification and reduce flip time to <60s (ETA 2028-07-30).
- (karthik_iyer) Coordinate the customer-facing postmortem delivery and set a short call to review findings (ETA 2028-07-16).

Attached: postmortem-summary-20280715.pdf (customer-facing), rw-traffic-shift-quicksteps.pdf (operator-facing).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Reliability Operations, Redwood Inference
